chapter: Fred Astaire and the high points
title: Rehearsing "St. James Infirmary" with Astaire as his shadow
summary: Astaire built a dance number to the recorded "St. James Infirmary" solo, featured Jones throughout and stood behind him copying his gestures; a hotel party watched the tape on televisions in every corner.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: It might sound like that but I don't do it that way every time. Now, I have to learn it over like the record because he says, "You've got to do this just like the record because I've got steps going with it." And he featured me all the way through. Not like they used to throw you out there and do two numbers and that's all. I did a sketch with him. I played my hit things. And then I was in the "St. James Infirmary." "St. James Infirmary," was the big number of the show, and he was standing behind me, singing, and he said, "I'm going to be your shadow, instead of," we were turning around from Ted Lewis.
And I'm going through all this, you know, and rubbing and blowing on my fingers, and he's doing it behind me.

And it was real nice. And then he took us all to the hotel and had a room with a television in each corner, because they had to play it back for the east coast. See they had to play it back. What you saw was the tape. They did it live in California. And then when it come time for it to play here -- or else they did it live here, I think. It come through here live, and for California, it had to come on --
Yeah, on account of the time difference. And we was doing it out there, which was about 7:00 o'clock. That would have been 10:00 o'clock here or something.
So then for it to come into California at 10:00 or 9:00, they had to do it again, but they showed the tape, and he had a big party in this big room in a hotel.
All the food and the TV in each corner of the room.
And everybody sitting there, looking at it, you know.
And gloating over what's happening, you know.
